learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the history of trade in India, the nature and purpose of business, and the classification of business activities!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Economic activities are performed to earn a livelihood (like a doctor treating patients or a shopkeeper selling goods). Non-economic activities are performed out of love, sympathy, or affection (like a mother cooking for her children).
Business is an economic activity involving the regular production or procurement of goods and services to sell them and earn a profit, all while taking on an element of risk.
Business activities are divided into Industry (production/processing of goods like manufacturing cars) and Commerce (activities that facilitate trade, like transport, banking, and warehousing).
Risk is the possibility of inadequate profits or even losses due to uncertainties (like a change in fashion, natural disasters, or strikes). Profit is considered the 'reward' for bearing this risk!

fun_activity.title: 🕵️‍♂️ The Activity Detective
fun_activity.instructions: Look around your house! Your dad going to the office = Employment. Your local clinic doctor = Profession. The grocery store owner downstairs = Business. Your sibling helping you with homework = Non-economic activity. Classify 5 more activities you see today!

exam_tips: 📌 Always use the 'Profit Motive' and 'Regularity of Dealings' to differentiate business from a casual transaction (e.g., selling your old bike once is NOT a business).
📌 Learn the difference between Primary, Secondary, and Tertiary industries with at least two examples for each.
📌 'Auxiliaries to Trade' (transport, banking, insurance, warehousing, advertising) remove hindrances of place, time, risk, finance, and information.
quick_recap: ⭐ The primary objective of any business is survival, profit, and growth, but it also has social objectives like providing quality goods.
⭐ Hundi was a popular indigenous banking instrument used in ancient India for trade and credit.
⭐ Business risks are of two types: Speculative (chance of both profit and loss) and Pure (only chance of loss or no loss).
